items.title: Box Office: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Roars With $31 Million Debut, ‘Cat in the Hat’ Fizzles With $20 Million
items.summary:
"Godzilla Minus Zero" opened to $31.6 million from 3,254 North American theaters this weekend, the largest domestic opening ever for a live-action foreign-language film. The Toho production, distributed stateside by Gkids, overtook the record set in 2002 by the Chinese martial arts epic "Hero," which debuted to $17.8 million. Warner Bros.' animated "The Cat in the Hat" finished behind it with $20 million from 4,003 locations.

Variety reported that premium formats drove an unusual share of the Godzilla business. The film is the first Japanese production shot for Imax, and Imax screens alone delivered $12.7 million, or 40% of the domestic total; premium large formats including Dolby accounted for 74% of ticket sales, compared with 53% for "The Odyssey." Reviews and exit polling were strong, with a 90% on Rotten Tomatoes and an A CinemaScore. "We're so happy to see audiences embrace 'Godzilla Minus Zero' at an unprecedented scale for an international film," said Chance Huskey, VP of distribution for Gkids.

Takashi Yamazaki's film picks up two years after 2023's "Godzilla Minus One," with the creature regenerating to face a new monster in postwar Japan. The earlier installment opened to $11.4 million, finished with $57 million domestically and $113 million worldwide, and won the visual effects Oscar. "This weekend's opening takes the Japanese production to a new level," said David A. Gross of the newsletter FranchiseRe.

"The Cat in the Hat," with Bill Hader voicing the title character, drew an A CinemaScore but a 45% on Rotten Tomatoes, and added only $10 million from 60 international markets for a $30.5 million global start. The film cost $92 million. It arrives during a punishing stretch for Warner Bros., recently merged with Paramount Skydance, which has absorbed heavy theatrical losses on "Digger," "The Bride!" and "Supergirl."

The soft debut stands out because the film faced no family competition; Universal's "Forgotten Island" in September was the last major option for young audiences, and Disney and Pixar's original "Hoppers" opened to $45 million this spring. Gross expects the film to recoup in digital, streaming and TV licensing rather than theaters.

The weekend totaled $114 million across all releases, up 86% from the frame a year ago when "Predator: Badlands" led. Year-to-date revenue stands at $8.6 billion, 20% ahead of 2025, per Rentrak. Searchlight's "Wild Horse Nine," Martin McDonagh's dark comedy with John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell, opened eighth with $6 million from 1,100 theaters.

items.title: ‘SNL’ Weekend Update Brutally Roasts Elon Musk Over ‘Epic’ Midterms Defeat
items.summary:
"Saturday Night Live" sent Elon Musk to the Weekend Update desk this week, with featured player Jeremy Culhane playing the billionaire as a man incapable of discussing the results of Tuesday's midterm elections. Anchor Colin Jost opened with the number: "Elon, you've been in the news because you wasted half a billion dollars on the midterms."

The sketch, recapped by Variety, built on Musk's reported spending of nearly $500 million on Republican candidates, much of it in Texas, where most statewide races went to Democrats. Culhane's Musk deflected every question back to a single talking point. "No, I'm in the news because my car did a flip," he said. "It was like a freaking Hot Wheel."

Jost pressed him on Tesla halting Cybertruck production, another Texas story from the week, and got the same answer. "Hey, remember when my car did a flip? It was epic," Culhane's Musk replied, before drifting into a fantasy about hanging out with Jost and Michael Che and a leather jacket that turns into armor. "I cannot believe you are the richest person in the world," Jost said.

The segment's sharpest stretch came when Jost laid out the sequence plainly: Musk left California because Democrats ran it, moved his companies to Texas to avoid taxes, built his own town there, and now finds Texas run by Democrats. "Ouchie! Ouchie! That is another epic vulgar roast from Colin Jost, my poorest friend," Culhane's Musk answered.

The bit closed with Musk explaining that an "epic vulgar roast" is a feature of his AI, Grok, then asking it to turn on him. Among the lines: "Elon Musk, you're the worst thing South Africa has ever done." Culhane's Musk fled the desk shouting for Grok to shut down.

items.title: Emma Stone Joins Druski During His ‘SNL’ Hosting Debut
items.summary:
Druski hosted "Saturday Night Live" this weekend, and he used his monologue to point out what the booking represented: he is the first online content creator to host the show. The comedian, whose real name is Drew Desbordes, brought Emma Stone onstage partway through, and The Strokes performed as musical guest.

Druski worked through the framing himself. "Apparently, people are saying I'm the first internet content creator, social media influencer, only make you laugh on your phone, TikTok and YouTube and Instagram star to host this show," he said, adding that the show gave him two rules — no cussing, no whiteface — neither of which he promised to follow. His family sat in the audience, and when he wondered aloud how to repay them, one of them called out, "Some money!"

Stone joined him to talk about "The Catch," the Universal rom-com they shot together. Druski described himself as her love interest, and Stone corrected him. "I think you might have misread that in those scenes because we weren't love interests in the film, but now it is actually starting to make more sense to me why you kept looking at me like that," she said. The film, directed by Stone's husband Dave McCary, a former "SNL" segment director, opens May 21, 2027.

The Hollywood Reporter noted that the episode also spoofed Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's Elizabeth Holmes documentary "You Can See Everything," imagining Druski as the original director. Jane Wickline played Holmes and Ben Marshall played Billy Evans, with Druski eventually donning prosthetics to play Holmes himself. Texas senator-elect James Talarico appeared in the cold open, telling James Austin Johnson's Trump that viewers want something different from the show's political sketches.

Druski built his following through online sketches before moving into television with "Grown-ish" and film with "House Party," and he hosted the BET Awards in June. On Monday, he signed a multi-year deal with Netflix, starting with the semi-scripted comedy series "Collect Praise." Season 52 has already featured Jalen Brunson, Dakota Johnson, Shane Gillis and Inde Navarrette as hosts; John Mulaney hosts the Nov. 14 episode with Phoebe Bridgers.
